subtopics.title: Introduction to the Link Layer
subtopics.summary: The basic service of moving network-layer datagrams between adjacent nodes via framing/encapsulation; the services provided (link access, reliable delivery, error detection) and where the link layer is implemented (network adapters/NICs); broadcast vs. point-to-point links.

subtopics.title: Error-Detection and -Correction Techniques
subtopics.summary: Techniques for detecting and correcting transmission errors in link-layer frames: simple and two-dimensional parity checks, checksumming methods, and the cyclic redundancy check (CRC).

subtopics.title: Multiple Access Protocols
subtopics.summary: Coordinating access to a shared broadcast channel using three broad approaches: channel partitioning (TDM, FDM), random access (ALOHA, CSMA, CSMA/CD), and taking-turns (polling, token passing); DOCSIS as the link-layer protocol for cable Internet access.

subtopics.title: Link-Layer Addressing and ARP
subtopics.summary: Link-layer (MAC) addresses, how they differ from network-layer addresses, and why broadcast channels require node addressing; address resolution between IP and MAC addresses.

subtopics.title: Ethernet and Link-Layer Switches
subtopics.summary: Ethernet framing and link-layer technologies; how link-layer switches forward and filter frames (e.g., self-learning) and their role compared with routers.

subtopics.title: Virtual LANs (VLANs)
subtopics.summary: Creating multiple virtual LANs over a single physical LAN infrastructure, including VLAN configuration and traffic isolation.

subtopics.title: MPLS and Data Center Networking
subtopics.summary: How MPLS networks provide link-layer services when interconnecting IP routers, and an overview of network designs for today's massive data centers.
